name: Bihar

topAttractions.name: Bodh Gaya
topAttractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage sites, where Lord Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree.

topAttractions.name: Nalanda University
topAttractions.description: A historic university and one of the oldest centers of learning in the world, which was a major hub of Buddhist and Hindu learning in ancient India.

topAttractions.name: Vaishali
topAttractions.description: An ancient city and a major pilgrimage site for Buddhists and Jains, which is home to the Ashokan Pillar and the Vaishali Stupa.

bestTimeToVisit: October to February, when the weather is cool and pleasant, making it ideal for sightseeing and outdoor activities.
culturalFact: Bihar is home to the ancient tradition of Madhubani painting, a unique and intricate form of folk art that originated in the Mithila region and is now a Geographical Indication (GI)-tagged craft.

hiddenGem.name: Valmiki National Park
hiddenGem.description: A lesser-known wildlife sanctuary that is home to a wide variety of flora and fauna, including the Bengal tiger, and offers opportunities for trekking and birdwatching.

relatedFestival: Bodh Purnima, a festival that celebrates the enlightenment of Lord Buddha, which is observed in January at Bodh Gaya.
passportTieIn: If you have a stamp from Bodh Gaya, you might also want to visit the nearby Mahabodhi Temple, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major pilgrimage site for Buddhists.
